the DNA damage signaling kinase, ATR and its scaffold protein, ATR-Interacting Protein (ATRIP) are required for efficient replication of herpes simplex virus 1, but that activation of the kinase does not affect virus yield.
all of the ATR signaling components are recruited to HSV-1 replication compartments and are required for efficient virus replication.

the cellular DNA damage response pathway proteins ATRIP, Claspin and RPA70, as well as the DNA damage response pathway protein TopBP1, are all required for efficient replication of herpes simplex virus 1.

the interplay between the DNA damage response (DDR) and herpesvirus replication.
the interplay between the host and the virus during HSV-1 infection.
the role that the cellular ATR pathway plays during HSV-1 infection.

the ATR pathway is not antiviral but that activation of this pathway prior to infection may have negative consequences, such as inhibitory effects on viral recombination.
